identity.title: CAX: Cellular Automata Accelerated in JAX

problem.claim: Enable faster, more flexible, and reproducible exploration of cellular automata across scientific applications.

gap.claim: The authors identify the lack of a hardware-accelerated cellular-automata library as limiting research directions, collaboration, and reproducibility.

contributions.claim: Introduces CAX, a high-performance, flexible, open-source cellular-automata library built in JAX.
Provides a modular, user-friendly interface supporting discrete and continuous cellular automata in arbitrary dimensions.
Presents three cellular-automata experiments implemented in a few lines of code using the library’s modular architecture.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CAX as a hardware-accelerated, modular library intended to broaden cellular-automata research, including support for discrete and continuous models of any dimensionality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CAX speeds simulations by up to 2,000× across examples ranging from elementary cellular automata and Conway’s Game of Life to growing neural cellular automata and self-classifying MNIST digits.
The authors report three novel cellular-automata experiments implemented in only a few lines of code.
The authors report that a simple one-dimensional cellular automaton outperforms GPT-4 on the 1D-ARC challenge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cellular automata are used to study emergence and self-organization across several disciplines.
The authors link limited exploration, collaboration, and reproducibility to the absence of hardware-accelerated library support.
CAX is introduced as an accelerated, flexible, open-source library with modular support for discrete and continuous models in any number of dimensions.
Benchmarks, applications, three compact experiments, and a 1D-ARC comparison are used to illustrate performance and research potential.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a reusable system contribution with concrete benchmarks, varied applications, compact experiments, and a task-specific comparison.

lessons.interpretation: A systems paper can make its research-enabling claim more tangible by connecting infrastructure properties to both performance and downstream use cases.
lessons.application: Frame a tool contribution around a small set of representative workloads, a quantitative performance result, and one demonstration of how its design lowers experimentation effort.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when workloads are not comparable or when speed and implementation brevity are not the intended contribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify hardware, baselines, benchmark settings, or whether the reported 2,000× speedup is typical or an upper bound.
Details and evaluation criteria for the three experiments and the 1D-ARC comparison are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independently verified correctness, reproducibility, or priority of the claimed novelty.
